mainTopic: The decline after שמעון הצדיק's death, Temple miracles, and whether drawing the lots on יום הכפורים is essential
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a greedy כהן nicknamed חמצן, and two אמוראים bring פסוקים showing that this word means 'robber.' A ברייתא then tells how שמעון הצדיק knew from a changed vision on יום הכפורים that he would die that year. After his death, the כהנים stopped blessing with the שם המפורש. In the last forty years before the חורבן, the good signs in the בית המקדש stopped, and the היכל doors opened by themselves until רבן יוחנן בן זכאי rebuked them. This leads to explanations of why the Temple is called לבנון and יער, including שלמה's golden fruit trees. The גמרא then returns to the משנה: the כהן גדול says the שם ten times on יום הכפורים, and a list of miracles follows about Temple sounds and smells that reached far away. Finally, רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן argue whether drawing the lots is essential. The גמרא gives two versions of how their argument fits רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה, and it begins a challenge from a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The greedy כהן keeps the nickname 'robber' for life
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of the ברייתא about the greedy כהן: people called him חמצן until the day he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: [They called him] 'robber' until the day of his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא on the previous amud: a כהן who grabbed his own portion and his friend's portion was called חמצן for the rest of his life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nickname was a lasting public mark of shame for his greed. The odd word חמצן sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks for a פסוק that shows this word means 'robber.'

keyTerms.meaning: A robber or grabber; a nickname given to the greedy כהן
Until the day of his death

steps.confusionAlert: חמצן has nothing to do with חמץ on פסח (leavened bread). Here the root means robbing or taking by force, as the next steps prove.

phrases.english: 'robber' until the day of his death.
phrases.notes: End of a sentence that began on the previous amud: 'they called him בן חמצן'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from the previous section of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The greedy כהן was publicly called חמצן for his whole life.

steps.title: A verse from תהלים shows that חומץ means robber
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר שילא brings a פסוק from תהלים in which חומץ appears next to 'wicked' and 'unrighteous,' showing that it means a robber.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר שילא said: What is the source? 'My God, rescue me from the hand of the wicked, from the grip of the unrighteous and the robber (חומץ).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we see that חמצן means robber, and רבה בר בר שילא answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, חומץ is listed together with רשע and מעול, words for evil people who harm others. That context shows חומץ means someone who takes by force, which explains the nickname חמצן.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (a request for a source in תנ״ך)

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Sheila said:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the second 'בר' in round brackets, so his name is just רבה בר שילא.

phrases.english: What is the verse [showing this meaning]?
'My God, rescue me from the hand of the wicked,
from the grip of the unrighteous and the robber.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק showing the meaning of the word חמצן from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The root חמץ means robber, as seen in the phrase 'מעול וחומץ.'

steps.title: רבא brings a different verse from ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a פסוק from ישעיהו that tells us to strengthen the חמוץ (the person who was robbed), which implies that we should not strengthen the חומץ (the robber).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The source is from here: 'Learn to do good, seek justice, strengthen the robbed one.' Strengthen the robbed one, but do not strengthen the robber.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a second source for the same word meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads חמוץ as the victim of robbery and the active form חומץ as the robber himself. The פסוק says to support the victim, which implies the opposite for the robber. This again shows that the root means robbing.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who was robbed (the victim)

phrases.english: Rava said: From here:
'Learn to do good, seek justice,
strengthen the robbed one.'
Strengthen the robbed one,
but do not strengthen the robber.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same point as רבה בר בר שילא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמוץ is the one who was robbed and חומץ is the robber, so חמצן means robber.
steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים agree that חמצן means robber; they only disagree about which פסוק is the source.

steps.title: שמעון הצדיק announces that he will die this year
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: in the year he died, שמעון הצדיק told his colleagues that 'he' would die that year, speaking indirectly about himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: In the year that שמעון הצדיק died, he said to them: This year, he will die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ברייתא about the death of שמעון הצדיק. This sets up the next question: how did he know?
steps.deeperAnalysis: He says 'he will die' instead of 'I will die.' This is a polite way of avoiding saying something bad directly about oneself. The story explains the background to the changes in the בית המקדש described before and after it.

keyTerms.meaning: A great כהן גדול in the early Second Temple period

steps.confusionAlert: 'He will die' refers to שמעון הצדיק himself. He is speaking about himself in the third person.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה שֶׁמֵּת בָּהּ שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק,
phrases.english: In the year in which Shimon HaTzaddik died,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: בְּשָׁנָה זוֹ הוּא מֵת.
phrases.english: he said to them: In this year, he will die.
phrases.notes: An indirect way of referring to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אוֹתָהּ שָׁנָה שֶׁמֵּת בָּהּ שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ברייתא about שמעון הצדיק's death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמעון הצדיק predicted his own death in that year.

steps.title: His colleagues ask how he knows
steps.stepSummary: The people around him ask שמעון הצדיק how he knows that he will die this year.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: How do you know?
steps.whatsHappening: His colleagues ask how he knows, which sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question is part of the story itself. It is not a challenge to his claim. It invites him to describe the sign he saw.

phrases.english: They said to him: How do you know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the prediction in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sign showed שמעון הצדיק that he would die this year?

steps.title: The vision of the old man in white and in black
steps.stepSummary: Every יום הכפורים, an old man dressed in white went into the קודש הקדשים with him and came out with him. This year, an old man dressed in black went in with him but did not come out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Every יום הכפורים an old man met me, dressed in white and wrapped in white. He went in with me and came out with me. But today an old man met me, dressed in black and wrapped in black. He went in with me but did not come out with me.
steps.whatsHappening: שמעון הצדיק explains that a change in a vision he saw every year in the קודש הקדשים told him that his death was near.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White is a sign of life and good fortune, and black is a sign of mourning. In earlier years the figure 'left with him,' a sign that he would come through safely. This year the figure did not leave with him, which signaled that his life was ending.

keyTerms.meaning: The day the כהן גדול enters the קודש הקדשים
An old man (seen in a vision)

phrases.english: He said to them: On every Yom Kippur
an old man would meet me,
dressed in white and wrapped in white;
he would go in with me and come out with me.
phrases.notes: Into the קודש הקדשים and back out.

phrases.english: But today an old man met me,
dressed in black and wrapped in black;
he went in with me but did not come out with me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The change from a figure in white who left with him to a figure in black who did not leave with him was a sign of his coming death.

steps.title: He falls ill after סוכות and dies
steps.stepSummary: The prediction comes true: after the רגל of סוכות, שמעון הצדיק was ill for seven days and died.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the festival, he was ill for seven days and died.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us how the story ends: his prediction came true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'רגל' here is סוכות, which comes a few days after יום הכפורים. His death soon after confirms what the vision had shown him.
steps.whatToRemember: שמעון הצדיק knew from the changed vision on יום הכפורים that he would die, and he died shortly after סוכות.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר הָרֶגֶל חָלָה שִׁבְעָה יָמִים וָמֵת.
phrases.english: After the festival he was ill for seven days and died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַר הָרֶגֶל חָלָה שִׁבְעָה יָמִים וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the prediction from steps 4 to 6 came true.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The vision was correct: שמעון הצדיק died that year, after סוכות.

steps.title: After his death the כהנים stop blessing with God's explicit Name
steps.stepSummary: After שמעון הצדיק died, his fellow כהנים stopped saying the שם המפורש in ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his brothers, the כהנים, stopped blessing with the Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins describing a change that happened after שמעון הצדיק's death. The explanation of this change continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he was alive, the כהנים said the explicit four-letter Name in ברכת כהנים. After his death they held back, apparently because the generation was less worthy. This adds to the list of things that declined after his passing.

keyTerms.meaning: His brothers, the כהנים (his fellow כהנים)
To bless with God's explicit Name (in ברכת כהנים)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one great צדיק's presence affected the spiritual level of the whole בית המקדש. His death caused a lasting change in how ברכת כהנים was said.

phrases.english: And his brothers, the priests, refrained
from blessing with the [explicit] Name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes a result of the death reported in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After שמעון הצדיק's death, the כהנים no longer said the שם המפורש in ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: Three good signs stopped forty years before the destruction
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that in the last forty years before the חורבן, three positive signs stopped happening.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Forty years before the Temple was destroyed, the lot for ה׳ never came up in the כהן גדול's right hand, the red strip did not turn white, and the western lamp did not stay lit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists three good signs that stopped in the last forty years before the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the time of שמעון הצדיק, these signs showed that ה׳ accepted the עבודה. The lot for ה׳ came up in the right hand, the red strip turned white to show forgiveness, and the נר מערבי kept burning. Now all three fail, which shows that Heaven no longer looked favorably on the people.

keyTerms.meaning: The lot drawn on יום הכיפורים to decide which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל
In the right hand, a good sign
A strip of crimson (red) wool that turned white as a sign of forgiveness
The western lamp of the מנורה, which miraculously kept burning
The destruction of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the lot came up in the left hand by pure chance once in a while. The point is that it never came up on the right even once in forty years, which is a clear sign from Heaven.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Forty years before the destruction of the Temple
the lot (for ה׳) did not come up in the right hand,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה לָשׁוֹן שֶׁל זְהוֹרִית מַלְבִּין,
phrases.english: and the strip of crimson wool did not turn white,
and the western lamp did not burn.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה קוֹדֶם חוּרְבַּן הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the decline after שמעון הצדיק's death and describes the final low point before the חורבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the last forty years before the חורבן, the lot, the red strip, and the נר מערבי all stopped showing Heaven's favor.

steps.title: The Temple doors open by themselves and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי rebukes them
steps.stepSummary: The doors of the היכל kept opening on their own as a sign of the coming destruction, until רבן יוחנן בן זכאי rebuked them and quoted זכריה's prophecy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The doors of the היכל would open by themselves, until רבן יוחנן בן זכאי scolded them. He said: 'היכל, היכל! Why are you frightening yourself? I know that you will be destroyed in the end. זכריה בן עדוא already prophesied about you: "Open your doors, O לבנון, so that fire may consume your cedars."'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a fourth, frightening sign: the היכל doors opened by themselves. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי tells the היכל that it does not need to keep warning everyone, because its destruction is already known from a נבואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doors opening on their own hinted that enemies would soon walk right in. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי proves from the verse in זכריה that the destruction had already been foretold. That verse calls the Temple 'לבנון', and this name sets up the next steps, which explain the Temple's nicknames.

keyTerms.meaning: The main sanctuary building of the בית המקדש
Literally the Lebanon mountains; used here as a name for the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: The verse's use of 'לבנון' for the Temple is the bridge to the next two statements, which explain why the Temple has this name.

phrases.english: And the doors of the Sanctuary would open by themselves,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁגָּעַר בָּהֶן רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי.
phrases.english: until Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai scolded them.
He said to it: Sanctuary, Sanctuary!
Why do you frighten yourself?

phrases.aramaic: יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי בְּךָ שֶׁסּוֹפְךָ עָתִיד לֵיחָרֵב,
phrases.english: I know about you that you will ultimately be destroyed,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְבָר נִתְנַבֵּא עָלֶיךָ זְכַרְיָה בֶּן עִדּוֹא:
phrases.english: and Zechariah son of Iddo already prophesied about you:
"Open your doors, O Lebanon, that fire may devour your cedars."
phrases.notes: זכריה 11:1. Here 'לבנון' refers to the בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another bad sign to the list in the same ברייתא and supports it with a prophetic verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Temple's destruction was already foretold by זכריה, who called the Temple 'לבנון'.

steps.title: Why the Temple is called 'לבנון'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בן טבלאי explains that the Temple is called לבנון because it 'whitens' the sins of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בן טבלאי said: Why is the Temple called לבנון? Because it makes the sins of ישראל white.
steps.whatsHappening: The verse just quoted called the Temple 'לבנון'. Now the גמרא brings an explanation of that name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name לבנון shares a root with 'לבן' (white). The קרבנות and עבודה in the Temple wash sins clean, like turning something stained into white. This matches the idea of the red strip turning white from step 9.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak ben Tavlai said:
Why is it (the Temple) called Lebanon?
Because it whitens the sins of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word 'לבנון' that appeared in the verse quoted in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Temple is called לבנון because it whitens (atones for) ישראל's sins.

steps.title: Why the Temple is called 'Forest'
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה explains that the Temple is called 'יער' (forest) because, like a forest, it blooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said: Why is the Temple called a forest, as it says 'the house of the forest of לבנון'? To teach you that just as a forest blooms, the בית המקדש also blooms.
steps.whatsHappening: A second nickname for the Temple is explained. It is called 'יער' (forest) because it blooms like a forest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for the name is the פסוק 'בית יער הלבנון'. The comparison is that a forest grows and blossoms, and so does the Temple. The next step shows that this blooming was literal.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The house of the forest of Lebanon', a פסוק in מלכים

phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviya said:
Why is it (the Temple) called Forest,
as it is written: "The house of the forest of Lebanon"?
To tell you: just as a forest blooms,
so too the Temple blooms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second nickname explanation, parallel to step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Temple is called יער because, like a forest, it blooms.

steps.title: שלמה's golden fruit trees prove the Temple 'bloomed'
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא's statement supports the 'blooming' idea: שלמה planted golden fruit trees in the Temple, and they really produced fruit, which supported the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הושעיא said: When שלמה built the בית המקדש, he planted in it all kinds of sweet fruit trees made of gold. They produced fruit in their proper season. When the wind blew on them, their fruit would fall, as it says: 'His fruit will rustle like לבנון.' These fruits were a source of income for the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב הושעיא's statement as a proof that the Temple truly 'bloomed', as רב זוטרא בר טוביה said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The golden trees miraculously produced real fruit in season, so the 'blooming' was literal and not just a nice image. The פסוק 'ירעש כלבנון פריו' ties fruit to 'לבנון', the Temple's name. The fallen golden fruit also provided income for the כהונה.
steps.whatToRemember: The Temple has two nicknames. It is called לבנון because it whitens sins, and יער because it blooms. The blooming was literal, through שלמה's golden fruit trees, which also supported the כהנים.

phrases.english: As Rav Hoshaya said:
When Solomon built the Temple,

phrases.aramaic: נָטַע בּוֹ כׇּל מִינֵי מְגָדִים שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: he planted in it all kinds of sweet fruit (trees) of gold,
and they would produce fruit in their season.
And when the wind would blow on them,
their fruits would fall off,
as it is stated: "May his fruit rustle like Lebanon,"
and from them there was a livelihood for the priesthood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 12's claim that the Temple 'blooms' with a literal account.
steps.raayaObject: רב זוטרא בר טוביה's statement that the בית המקדש blooms like a forest
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הושעיא's account of שלמה's golden fruit trees, together with the פסוק 'ירעש כלבנון פריו'

steps.title: The golden trees withered and will one day return
steps.stepSummary: When the גוים entered the היכל, שלמה's golden trees dried up. In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will restore them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the nations entered the היכל, the trees dried up, as it says: 'The blossom of לבנון withers.' In the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will give it back to us, as it says: 'It will blossom fully and rejoice... the glory of לבנון will be given to it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב הושעיא's teaching about the golden fruit trees. It tells us what happened to them at the חורבן and what will happen in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said the trees really gave fruit. Now we learn this lasted only while the היכל stood in holiness. Once גוים entered, the trees dried up (נחום). Then a פסוק in ישעיה promises that the 'blossoming of לבנון', meaning the Temple, will come back.

keyTerms.meaning: to return it / to restore it

steps.whatToRemember: The Temple is called לבנון and יער because it 'blooms'. The blooming stopped at the חורבן and will return with the גאולה.

phrases.english: And once the nations entered the Sanctuary
they (the golden trees) dried up,
as it says: 'And the blossom of Lebanon withers.'
phrases.notes: נחום א:ד. 'Lebanon' here means the Temple.

phrases.english: And in the future the Holy One, Blessed be He,
will give it back to us,
as it says: 'It will surely blossom,
and rejoice, with joy and singing;
the glory of Lebanon will be given to it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes רב הושעיא's statement about the golden trees from step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The golden trees dried up when the גוים entered the היכל and will be restored in the future, based on פסוקים in נחום and ישעיה.

steps.title: The כהן גדול says God's Name ten times on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about placing the lots on the two goats. It then brings a ברייתא: the כהן גדול mentions the שם ten times that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He placed them on the two goats.' The Rabbis taught: The כהן גדול mentions the Name ten times on that day: three in the first confession, three in the second confession, three over the goat sent away, and one with the lots.
steps.whatsHappening: The אגדה side-trip is over, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה. When the כהן גדול places the lot, he says 'לה׳ חטאת'. So the גמרא brings a ברייתא counting every time he says the שם that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lot gives us one mention of the שם. The ברייתא adds up the full total of ten: 3 + 3 in the two וידויים over his פר, 3 over the שעיר המשתלח, and 1 at the גורלות.

keyTerms.meaning: the goat sent away to עזאזל

steps.confusionAlert: There are two confessions over the פר (first for himself and his house, second including the כהנים). The third set is over a different animal, the שעיר המשתלח. Don't think all three confessions are over the same animal.

phrases.english: 'He placed them on the two goats.'
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה, starting a new topic.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught (in a ברייתא):
Ten times the High Priest mentions
the Name (of God) on that day:
three in the first confession,
and three in the second confession,
and three over the goat that is sent away,
and one with the lots.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְתָנָן עַל שְׁנֵי הַשְּׂעִירִים. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה about the Temple and returns to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול says the שם ten times on יום הכפורים: 3 + 3 + 3 in the three וידויים and 1 at the lots.

steps.title: The כהן גדול's voice was heard all the way in יריחו
steps.stepSummary: Once, when the כהן גדול said the שם, his voice was heard in יריחו. רבה בר בר חנה adds that יריחו is ten פרסאות from ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And once he said 'the Name', and his voice was heard in יריחו. רבה בר בר חנה said: From ירושלים to יריחו is ten פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the topic of saying the שם, the גמרא tells of a miracle: the כהן גדול's voice carried all the way to יריחו. Then an אמורא tells us the distance, so we understand how big the miracle was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line by itself does not tell us how far יריחו is. רבה בר בר חנה fills this in: ten פרסאות, which is about forty מיל. Hearing a human voice that far is clearly a נס.

phrases.english: And once he said 'the Name',
and his voice was heard in Jericho.
Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
From Jerusalem to Jericho is ten parasangs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְבָר אָמַר הַשֵּׁם וְנִשְׁמַע קוֹלוֹ בִּירִיחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ten mentions of the שם with a story about the miraculous strength of the כהן גדול's voice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול's voice saying the שם was miraculously heard in יריחו, ten פרסאות away.

steps.title: More Temple sounds and smells sensed far away
steps.stepSummary: A list of more miracles: the hinges of the היכל doors were heard eight תחומי שבת away, and the smell of the קטורת reached יריחו and filled ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The hinge of the היכל doors was heard from eight תחומי שבת away. Goats in יריחו would sneeze from the smell of the קטורת. Women in יריחו did not need perfume because of the smell of the קטורת. A כלה in ירושלים did not need to adorn herself with perfume because of the smell of the קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: After the story about the voice reaching יריחו, the גמרא lists similar wonders. These are sounds and smells from the בית המקדש that were noticed very far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First comes a sound: the door hinges heard eight תחומי שבת away (2,000 אמות each, about eight מיל). Then come three examples of the קטורת's smell. It reached יריחו strongly enough to make goats sneeze and to perfume the women. Inside ירושלים, a כלה needed no perfume at all.

keyTerms.meaning: the incense offered in the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The בית המקדש's holiness was felt far beyond its walls: the כהן גדול's voice, the doors' hinges, and the קטורת's smell all reached far-off places.

phrases.english: And the hinge of the doors of the Sanctuary
was heard from eight Shabbat limits away.
Goats that were in Jericho
would sneeze from the smell of the incense.
Women who were in Jericho
did not need to perfume themselves, because of the smell of the incense.
A bride who was in Jerusalem
did not need to adorn herself (with perfume), because of the smell of the incense.

steps.triggerLanguage: וָצִיר דַּלְתוֹת הַהֵיכָל נִשְׁמַע בִּשְׁמוֹנָה תְּחוּמֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the voice-in-יריחו miracle into a list of other Temple sounds and smells sensed far away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sound of the היכל's door hinges and the smell of the קטורת miraculously carried great distances, as far as יריחו.

steps.title: Goats sneezed from the incense smell
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן דולגאי reports that his father's goats in the hills of מכמר sneezed from the smell of the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן דולגאי said: My father had goats in the hills of מכמר, and they used to sneeze from the smell of the קטורת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list of miracles about the קטורת with an eyewitness family report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the smell of the קטורת reached יריחו. This step adds another sign of how far it spread. Goats far from ירושלים reacted to it physically.

keyTerms.meaning: The smell of the Temple incense

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben Dolgai said:
Father had goats in the hills of Mikhmar,
phrases.notes: A district some distance from ירושלים.

phrases.english: and they would sneeze from the smell of the incense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example to the list of incense miracles from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The smell of the קטורת was so strong that it made goats sneeze far from ירושלים.

steps.title: The incense smell still lingered in שילה
steps.stepSummary: An old man told רבי יהושע בן קרחה that he smelled קטורת between the walls of the ruined משכן in שילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: An old man told me that he once went to שילה and smelled the smell of קטורת coming from between its walls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more incense report. This one is about the smell lasting for a very long time, not about it traveling far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משכן in שילה was destroyed many centuries earlier. Even so, the smell of its קטורת was still noticeable. The previous reports were about distance, and this one adds the dimension of time.

keyTerms.meaning: שילה, where the משכן stood in the days of the שופטים

steps.whatToRemember: The miracle list ends here. The smell of the קטורת traveled far (to יריחו and the hills of מכמר) and lasted long (in שילה).

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said:
An old man reported to me:
One time I went to Shiloh,
and I smelled the smell of incense from between its walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final incense report, which closes the aggadic section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The smell of the קטורת of the משכן in שילה lingered long after it was destroyed.

steps.title: Is drawing the lot essential to the service?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי: drawing the lot from the box is essential, but placing it on the goat is not. רבי יוחנן: even drawing it is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: Pulling the lot out of the box is essential, but placing the lot on the goat is not essential. רבי יוחנן said: Even pulling the lot out is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the stories and returns to the halacha of the גורלות from the משנה. It quotes a dispute about which parts of the lottery are required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that placing the lot on the goat (הנחה) is not required. They argue only about pulling the lot out of the box (עליה). If it is not required, the goats can be designated even without the lottery. If it is required, skipping it would ruin the service.

keyTerms.meaning: The box or urn that holds the lots
Essential; without it the מצוה is invalid
Placing the lot on the goat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse 'not מעכב' with 'not a מצוה.' The lottery should still be done. The only question is whether the service is invalid if it was skipped.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
Drawing the lot from inside the receptacle is indispensable;
placing (the lots on the goats) is not indispensable.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even the drawing is not indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: עֲלִיַּית גּוֹרָל מִתּוֹךְ קַלְפִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's topic of the גורלות, quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ינאי: עליה is מעכב and הנחה is not. רבי יוחנן: neither is מעכב.

steps.title: According to רבי יהודה, everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, actions done in בגדי לבן outside the קודש הקדשים are not essential, so all agree the lottery is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה, who holds that things done in the white garments outside the קודש הקדשים are not essential, everyone agrees the lottery is not essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to locate where the dispute applies. First it shows a view under which there is no argument at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lottery is done in בגדי לבן, but outside the קודש הקדשים. רבי יהודה holds that outside actions like this are never מעכב. So under his view, even רבי ינאי would agree the lottery is not essential.

keyTerms.meaning: The white garments the כהן גדול wears for the special יום הכפורים service

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
matters performed in the white garments outside (the Holy of Holies)
are not indispensable —

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָא מְעַכְּבָא.
phrases.english: everyone agrees that it is not indispensable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the dispute from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי יהודה's view, the lottery is not מעכב according to everyone.

steps.title: The dispute follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The argument exists only according to רבי נחמיה. One side applies his rule to the lottery. The other says his rule covers only an עבודה, and the lottery is not an עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue according to רבי נחמיה. The one who says the lottery is essential simply follows רבי נחמיה. The one who says it is not essential holds that רבי נחמיה's rule applies only to a real Temple service, and the lottery is not a service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows exactly where רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן disagree and what each one is thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה holds that everything done in בגדי לבן is מעכב, even outside the קודש הקדשים. רבי ינאי applies this rule to the lottery, so for him it is מעכב. רבי יוחנן says the rule covers only an עבודה, and the הגרלה is not an עבודה, so for him it is not מעכב even according to רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole dispute depends on one question: is the הגרלה an עבודה? If yes, רבי נחמיה's rule makes it מעכב. If no, it is not מעכב.
steps.confusionAlert: Some printed translations say 'therefore it is indispensable' at the end of this step. The correct meaning is the opposite: because the הגרלה is not an עבודה, it is NOT מעכב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key distinction that appears across the Temple-service sugyos: a formal עבודה versus a procedural act that is not itself a service.

phrases.english: When they disagree, it is according to Rabbi Neḥemya:
The one who said it is indispensable holds like Rabbi Neḥemya.
And the one who said it is not indispensable (holds):
this (rule) applies only to a service;
the drawing of lots is not a service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 21 shows where there is no argument, this step shows where the argument really is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי נחמיה's view: רבי ינאי says the lottery is מעכב. רבי יוחנן says it is not, because הגרלה is not an עבודה.

steps.title: Introducing a second version of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא signals that some report the dispute in a different way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say (a different version):
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to present another version of how רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן's argument fits with רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איכא דאמרי means there was a second tradition about the same discussion. The content of that version comes next.

phrases.english: Some say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an alternative version of the analysis in steps 21 and 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a second tradition of the dispute. Its content continues next.

steps.title: Second version: according to רבי נחמיה everyone agrees the lottery is essential
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, according to רבי נחמיה, both אמוראים agree that the lottery is essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי נחמיה, who says these actions are essential, everyone agrees that the lottery is essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the second version that it announced in the last step. It begins by saying there is no argument at all according to רבי נחמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the argument was only according to רבי נחמיה. Here it is flipped: רבי נחמיה holds that actions done in בגדי לבן are essential, so both רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן agree the lottery is essential according to him. This sets up the next line, where the argument moves to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is essential; without it the service is not valid
Everyone agrees; there is no argument

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the first version, everyone agreed according to רבי יהודה (not essential). In this second version, everyone agrees according to רבי נחמיה (essential).

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Nechemya
who said it is essential
phrases.notes: He holds that every action done in בגדי לבן is essential, even outside the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: everyone agrees that it (the lottery) is essential,
phrases.notes: 'Everyone' means רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the second version of the dispute announced in Step 23, reversing the framing of Steps 21-22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נחמיה, all agree the lottery is essential.

steps.title: The argument is according to רבי יהודה, because the verse repeats 'אשר עלה'
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is according to רבי יהודה. One side applies his rule (not essential). The other says the lottery is an exception because the פסוק says 'אשר עלה' twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue according to רבי יהודה. The one who says it is not essential follows רבי יהודה's rule. The one who says it is essential says: here is different, because the פסוק repeats 'אשר עלה', 'אשר עלה', two times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where the argument is in the second version. It is according to רבי יהודה, and it gives each side's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה normally says that actions in בגדי לבן done outside the קודש הקדשים are not essential. One אמורא simply applies that rule to the lottery. The other agrees with the rule in general but makes an exception for the lottery, because the תורה repeats the phrase 'אשר עלה עליו הגורל' (ויקרא טז:ט, טז:י). A repeated phrase in the laws of קרבנות shows that something is essential.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different (an exception to the general rule)
The פסוק repeated it (said it a second time)
'Which came up' — from 'the goat on which the lot came up'

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a general rule (רבי יהודה's rule about בגדי לבן) can have an exception when the פסוק repeats itself. The repetition signals עיכוב (that the act is essential).

phrases.english: When they argue, it is according to Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר לָא מְעַכְּבָא — כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: The one who said it is not essential follows Rabbi Yehuda's rule,
and the one who said it is essential says:
here is different, because the verse repeated it:
'which came up', 'which came up', two times.
phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:ט and טז:י both say 'אשר עלה עליו הגורל'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second version by showing where the dispute is and the source for the stricter side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה: one view says the lottery is not essential; the other says it is essential because of the repeated 'אשר עלה'.
steps.whatToRemember: Second version: according to רבי נחמיה, all agree it is essential. According to רבי יהודה, they argue, and the stricter side relies on the double 'אשר עלה'.

steps.title: A ברייתא: drawing lots is a מצוה, but without it the service is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying the lottery is a מצוה, but if it was not done, the service is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: It is a מצוה to draw lots, and if he did not draw lots, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge the views it just presented. The ברייתא clearly says the lottery is not essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the lottery is a proper מצוה, but leaving it out does not ruin the service. That seems to contradict רבי ינאי, who said drawing the lot is essential. The next step checks which version of the dispute can still explain whose opinion this ברייתא follows.

phrases.english: They challenged: It is a מצוה to draw lots,
and if he did not draw lots, it is valid.
phrases.notes: For example, he assigned the goats by word, without the lots.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the positions just laid out.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's view that drawing the lot (עליה) is essential, especially as framed in the second version (steps 24-25), where he holds it is essential even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that without the lottery the service is valid, so the lottery is not essential. Any opinion that says it is essential must explain who the ברייתא follows.

steps.title: Under the first version, the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Under the first version, everyone agrees that according to רבי יהודה the lottery is not essential, so the ברייתא is simply רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well according to the version where you said that according to רבי יהודה everyone agrees it is not essential. Whose opinion is this ברייתא? It is רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts building its challenge by showing that the ברייתא fits the first version easily. It is setting up the next move, where it will ask how the second version can explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, both אמוראים agree that according to רבי יהודה the lottery is not essential. So the ברייתא ('if he did not draw, it is valid') matches רבי יהודה with no trouble. The 'בשלמא' wording tells us a difficulty is coming for the other version, where, according to רבי יהודה, one side says it is essential.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one side). A difficulty for the other side usually follows
Version (of how a dispute is reported)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not a full answer. 'בשלמא' only sets up the easy side; the real difficulty about the second version comes next.

phrases.english: Granted, according to that version
in which you said: according to Rabbi Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּלָא מְעַכְּבָא,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that it is not essential,
whose opinion is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the 'בשלמא' setup that sharpens the challenge from the ברייתא in Step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The second version (Steps 24-25), by contrast with the first version.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא fits the first version easily as רבי יהודה. This prepares the question of who the ברייתא could follow in the second version, where one side holds the lottery is essential even according to רבי יהודה.
